summary:
"The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.

Today's guests: Modupe Adegbembo, Jefferies, Economist; Marina Zavolock, Morgan Stanley, Chief European Equity Strategist; Majid Jafar, Crescent Petroleum CEO.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: MLB Labor Dispute Drives Record Short Interest in Braves Stock
summary: Short sellers are rapidly upping their bets against shares of the Atlanta Braves as contentious labor negotiations between Major League Baseball and its players union raise the prospects of a disruption to the 2027 season.

title: US Stock Futures Gain as Nasdaq 100 Looks to Snap Five-Day Slump
summary: US stock futures rose in early trading Friday, putting the Nasdaq 100 on track to end a five-day losing streak as yields hold steady and Bitcoin soars.

title: India’s Nuclear Opening Comes With a High Security Bar
summary: Investors seeking entry to the country’s atomic power sector will likely face scrutiny in one area above all others – their ability to safeguard critical infrastructure.

title: Post-Strike Movie Supply is Driving Theatre Demand, Vue Entertainment CEO says
summary: Vue Entertainment CEO Tim Richards says the chain may see its strongest summer box office since the pandemic. "What we are seeing this year is all the movies in the post-strike period now hitting out screens. But we are also seeing the studios and content-makers producing and releasing movies at unprecedented levels." He speaks to Bloomberg's Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie, and Skylar Montgomery Koning. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Week of Whiplash in Treasuries Is Closing With Traders on Pause
summary: After a turbulent stretch for the US bond market, traders are heading into Friday’s session with questions about what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s next move will be.

title: Everybody’s Business: Are We Headed For Stagflation?
summary: The Roosevelt Island Tram is a monument to the 1970s stagflation era when New York City ran out of money and couldn't borrow any more to build a subway between Manhattan and the island in the East River. On this episode of Everybody's Business, Stacey Vanek Smith and Allison Schrager ride the tram and talk stagflation: what is it and are we headed in that direction again? Listen to the full episode wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Turns Sour on Once-Buzzy Space Stock After 73% Rout
summary: Wall Street analysts are rushing to slash their price targets on spacecraft and satellites manufacturer York Space Systems Inc., saying the company’s path forward looks uncertain amid supply chain troubles and a slower pace of government contracts.

title: Stocks Rise as Bitcoin Rally Lifts Crypto Shares: Markets Wrap
summary: US equities advanced, with crypto-linked stocks among the biggest gainers as Bitcoin headed for its best week in more than three years. Treasuries trimmed early gains as oil wavered.

title: Gold Set for Third Weekly Gain on US Treasury Buyback Plans
summary: Gold was on track for a third weekly advance after the US Treasury’s unexpected ramp-up in buybacks of long-dated government debt underscored concerns about its fiscal burden.

title: Negative Economic Surprises Could Help Treasuries, HSBC’s Kettner Says
summary: Max Kettner, chief multi-asset strategist at HSBC, sees US growth momentum starting to slow down and says, “a streak of a couple of weeks uninterrupted of negative economic surprises” can bring back a bid for duration in US Treasuries. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hua Hong Grace, Weichai Power to Join Hong Kong Stock Benchmark
summary: Hang Seng Indexes Co. is adding Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor Ltd. and Weichai Power Co. to Hong Kong’s equity benchmark, the index compiler said following its quarterly review.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 21
summary: Oil headed for a significant weekly increase as traders awaited details on a US campaign to isolate Iran’s economy, with no apparent end in sight to a conflict that has slashed Middle East exports.

title: Euro-Zone Business Activity Sees Surprise Improvement
summary: Private-sector activity in the euro area unexpectedly improved slightly in August, thanks to the strongest manufacturing growth in more than four years. Bloomberg's Zoe Schneeweiss reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: RBI Deputy Gupta Sounds Upbeat on Economy, Sees 7% Growth
summary: India’s economy may outperform the central bank’s forecasts this financial year, according to Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta, as growth closer to 7% leaves policymakers watching for the need to raise borrowing costs if it further fans inflation.

title: BofA’s Hartnett Sees Pressure on Risk Assets If Bond Plan Fails
summary: A failure in the US Treasury’s plan to tame long-term bond yields would pressure the dollar and spur short bets against riskier assets in the lead-up to November midterm elections, according to Bank of America Corp. strategist Michael Hartnett.

title: Is Bessent Facing a Bond Market Credibility Issue?
summary: Jefferies Economist Modupe Adegbembo and Morgan Stanley Chief European Equity Strategist Marina Zavolock weigh the impact of US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's announcement that the department would at least double the size of its long-dated bond buybacks. They speak on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Making Battlefield Tech Fuels an 80% Rally for Swedish Stock
summary: A small Swedish firm is Europe’s best-performing defense stock in 2026, an ascent its chief executive puts down to a “third wave” of military spending that’s focused more on computer systems and drones than tanks and ammunition.

title: IMO Contradicts Trump Claims on Strait of Hormuz
summary: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez tells Bloomberg TV that the Strait of Hormuz is not open and that there is no confirmation that mines have been removed in the waterway, contradicting statements by US President Donald Trump. He says, "Until we have confirmation of demining and security that the vessels are not going to be attacked, I will not call for anyone in the area to take the risk to transit." (Source: Bloomberg)
